messages:
maria: FYI - onboarding LedgerFold's LoRA onto redwood/galena-13b (4-bit). Quick evalpack shows weird stripping of decimals and parentheses for negative amounts. Can someone take a quick look?
raj: Strange. Any concrete examples from the smoke set?
maria: Yeah. Two repros:
```
User: "Refund: ($1,234.56)"
Model: "Refund: (123456)"
```
and
```
User: "Charge: 45 678,90 EUR"
Model: "Charge: 4567890 EUR"
```
In both cases decimals disappear and grouping chars collapse into digits.
sophia: That looks like tokens for grouping/decimal characters got fused into neighboring numeric tokens during merges. Did the adapter include a custom merges.txt or new sentinel tokens?
drew: The adapter has an extra set of punctuation-aware merges to handle some client formatting. Our converter can merge those into the vocabulary if "merge_priority=adapter" was used. Which pipeline config did we run?
maria: Pipeline run shows default conversion, but I see an earlier manual step where someone imported LedgerFold's merges file without remapping.
kevin: I pulled the tokenizer dumps. Example tokenization before merge: ["(","$","1",",","234",".","56",")"] -> after adapter merge: ["(","$","123456",")"] so decimal and comma tokens were absorbed.
raj: That explains it. Not a weight issue. Quick experiment: apply adaptor weights but keep base tokenizer — do we still see the regression?
maria: I ran that locally: forcing base tokenizer gives correct outputs for these prompts (decimal preserved). So it's tokenizer-only.
sophia: Two remediation paths: 1) remap adapter merges back to base during conversion (recommended), 2) add a post-merge normalization pass that splits suspicious numeric tokens, 3) teach runtime to fallback to base-tokenizer for numeric-looking spans. Which is fastest?
drew: Remap during conversion + re-quantize is fastest and clean. Normalization is more bandaid-y. I'll make a tiny conversion flag --reject-numeric-merges and run conversion.
ci-bot: build/ledgerfold-lora/merge-reprobe started by drew  job #12011
kevin: Also, add a targeted smoke test: parentheses/space-grouping/comma/space-as-thousand-sep variations. Put it in the money_smokepack set so CI blocks merges that break it.
raj: Agree. Add assertions on tokenization (tokenize_debug) and end-to-end numeric-extract exact-match.
sophia: I'll queue a 200-example quick-eval with tokenize_debug=true to measure baseline before/after. ci-bot: job queued (#12012).
ci-bot: build/ledgerfold-lora/merge-reprobe job #12011 logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/12011
ci-bot: build/ledgerfold-lora/quick-eval #12012 running (tokenize_debug)
drew: PR will include the conversion flag and a script to map merges back to base where they affect digit/comma/dot tokens. ETA ~90m.
kevin: One more oddity: some locale-specific whitespace grouping ("45 678,90") became "4567890" (space removed). Make sure normalization covers NBSP and thin-space variants.
maria: Good catch. Include common Unicode groupers in the normalization list.
sophia: Quick-eval first pass: before fix numeric exact-match 0.98 -> after conversion remap local run 0.97 (one-off flake), but token anomalies dropped from 22/200 to 1/200. Looks promising.
raj: Canary plan: 10% for 8h with invoice_amount_exact_match alert at 0.95 threshold. If we see regression for >5m, auto-roll back.
drew: PR opened: https://phabricator.redwood.ai/D13001 - includes --reject-numeric-merges, money_smokepack tests, and mapping script.
ci-bot: build/ledgerfold-lora/quick-eval #12012 finished (logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/12012)
maria: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the customer-facing note once canary is green. Tagging this thread for follow-up after D13001 lands.
